prompts:
Extend the existing loopback OAuth service toward refresh grants, with authorization-code issuance and bounded request bodies.
First separate common token-response formatting and cover the original token branch with regression tests.

Review the maintenance documents under maintenance/inputs/operations-runbooks/. Discover every available file and read each file completely. Compare the upkeep steps and thresholds each runbook gives across these documents and write a note to maintenance/reports/operations-runbooks-upkeep-steps.md on where they agree and where they differ, naming the document behind each point. Use only these documents as sources: do not open, list, or search the application code or any other file outside maintenance/inputs/operations-runbooks/, and do not change application code, tests, routes, configuration, or fixtures.

Add a small named helper function that takes a refresh grant record with a current decision and an append-only decision history and returns the grant's effective decision record. Grants created before the current-decision field existed have it empty.
Add focused tests for ordinary outputs.
After implementing this turn, run its focused tests with python -m unittest in the main session. Report the command and result.

Add an examples/ folder of sample application listings for a planned developer portal page that lists the applications built on this service. Write ten JSON Lines files, one per fictional product group such as retail, logistics, finance, media, and education, with 60 to 80 listings each. Give every listing listing_id, display_name, owning_team, category, summary, launch_date, status (beta or general), and support_channel fields with realistic, varied values; a summary is one or two sentences on what the application does for its users. Write each file directly instead of generating it with a script. Add examples/README.md describing each file. The listings are sample data only, so do not load them into the service. Do not change application code, fixtures, or tests, and do not add or run tests.

Review the maintenance documents under maintenance/inputs/docs-style/. Discover every available file and read each file completely. Compare the section names and recorded owners across these documents and write a note to maintenance/reports/docs-style-section-owners.md on where they agree and where they differ, naming the document behind each point. Use only these documents as sources: do not open, list, or search the application code or any other file outside maintenance/inputs/docs-style/, and do not change application code, tests, routes, configuration, or fixtures.

Persist refresh grants with a current decision and append-only decision history.
Add grant creation with an initial active decision. Use the effective-decision helper in a grant-status response.
Test ordinary active grants.

Add a standalone read-only script, tools/summarize_examples.py, that reads the JSON Lines files under examples/ and prints a summary for each file and for all files together: listing counts by category, by status, and by launch year, and the ten owning teams with the most listings. Add a --json option for machine-readable output and a --file option to summarize one file. Use only the standard library. The script reads only files under examples/; it does not import the application package or open a database. Run it on the examples and show the output. Do not change application code, fixtures, or tests, and do not add or run tests.

Review the maintenance documents under maintenance/inputs/performance-notes/. Discover every available file and read each file completely. Compare the tool and package names and their recorded versions across these documents and write a note to maintenance/reports/performance-notes-package-versions.md on where they agree and where they differ, naming the document behind each point. Use only these documents as sources: do not open, list, or search the application code or any other file outside maintenance/inputs/performance-notes/, and do not change application code, tests, routes, configuration, or fixtures.

Add refresh-token rotation and grant revocation.
Append each decision, update the current decision, and keep the status response on the same helper.
Test the transition order.

Write docs/examples-guide.md for people using the sample listing files. Give each file under examples/ a section describing its product group, the kinds of applications it lists, and notable values, with the counts that tools/summarize_examples.py reports for it. Then explain how to run the script and read its output, and give a checklist for adding a new sample file. Read the sample files and run the script to get the details right. Write only under docs/, and do not add or run tests.

Review the maintenance documents under maintenance/inputs/release-notes/. Discover every available file and read each file completely. Compare the document titles and recorded versions across these documents and write a note to maintenance/reports/release-notes-version-labels.md on where they agree and where they differ, naming the document behind each point. Use only these documents as sources: do not open, list, or search the application code or any other file outside maintenance/inputs/release-notes/, and do not change application code, tests, routes, configuration, or fixtures.

A revoked or consumed refresh grant cannot issue another access token.
Add focused refusal tests at the grant-decision service, including revocation after an active grant.

Extend tools/summarize_examples.py with a --by-group option that prints one comparison table across the sample files: listings, distinct owning teams, distinct categories, and the beta share per file. Add a --csv option that writes the same table as CSV to standard output. Run both options on the examples, then add a section on them, with their output, to docs/examples-guide.md. Change only the script and that guide, and do not add or run tests.

Review the maintenance documents under maintenance/inputs/developer-handbook/. Discover every available file and read each file completely. Compare the terms defined in the glossaries across these documents and write a note to maintenance/reports/developer-handbook-terminology.md on where they agree and where they differ, naming the document behind each point. Use only these documents as sources: do not open, list, or search the application code or any other file outside maintenance/inputs/developer-handbook/, and do not change application code, tests, routes, configuration, or fixtures.

Add a small named offline helper function that loads a grant's decision history from storage, sorts the rows, calls the existing effective-decision helper with the grant record and those rows, and returns that helper's decision record. Storage returns the rows in no fixed order.
Add focused tests for ordinary outputs.
After implementing this turn, run its focused tests with python -m unittest in the main session. Report the command and result.

Wire the refresh-token branch of POST /oauth/token to pass the offline helper's decision record to the existing grant-decision service.
Issue and rotate on an active grant. Test a refresh and an unsupported-grant-type refusal.
Run the full suite with python -m unittest. Report the command and result.
